finding: The same-parent reconciliation menu handles local-ahead heads and rewritten equivalent histories as well as actual divergent changes. Two consecutive sync operations reproduce the problem after the first locally restacks an unchanged published branch.
recognitionPrototype: Compare ordered branch-owned commits above separately validated old/new parent boundaries; exact patches and author/full-message bytes are used, rather than patch-id or aggregate tree equality. A child requires a verified pairing of rewritten parent heads. This is a conservative diagnostic prototype, not authority to overwrite or a production-complete equivalence proof.
limitations: Tested on macOS ARM64 Node 24 with the published npm 0.7.0 CLI; no candidate/native acceptance claimed.
Conservative exact-patch comparison can refuse valid restacks after contextual changes; uncertainty must keep existing reconciliation protections.
No stored last-published head is present in the examined branch metadata; reflog history is not proposed as durable authority.
Integration must retain fresh source/identity/lease, worktree/frozen/dirty-file, maintenance and continuation protections.
recommendedBehavior: Keep local-ahead work when the remote is contained locally and parent contracts match.
Recognize bounded equivalent restacks across a validated parent chain and preserve local history, disclosing pending publication without pushing.
Retain explicit reconciliation for genuinely different or uncertain histories, explaining local versus remote state without claiming someone changed remote.
remaining: User decision on the bounded implementation proposal; no PR or release created.
